# Longest Alternating Subarray. -1 means no seesaw at all.

@example 6, 7, 6, 7, 6 rocks between 6 and 7; the drop to 5 ends it, and 5, 6 is only 2 long.
[6,7,6,7,6,5,6]
=> 5

@example From 9 the first step falls, so the longest seesaw starts one later: 8, 9, 8.
[9,8,9,8]
=> 3

@example No element is followed by a value 1 larger, so there is no seesaw.
[12,12,10,14]
=> -1

# Two elements, the second 1 larger, at the top of the value range.
[9999,10000]
=> 2

# Two elements, the second 1 smaller.
[2,1]
=> -1

# All equal.
[7,7,7,7]
=> -1

# Steps of +2.
[4,6,8]
=> -1

# Two rises in a row: the first seesaw stops at 2, and the next one starts
# at the second element of the rise (4, 5, 4, 5, 4, 5) and is the longest.
[7,3,4,5,4,5,4,5]
=> 6

# Every step rises by 1, so no seesaw is longer than 2.
[17,18,19,20,21]
=> 2

# The steps alternate but begin with a fall: the first element is left out.
[8,7,8,7,8]
=> 4

# Equal neighbours break a seesaw.
[1,2,2,1,2,1]
=> 3

# The longest seesaw ends at the last element.
[30,31,40,41,40,41]
=> 4

# Values on both sides of 255 and 256.
[255,256,255,256]
=> 4

# 100 elements, one seesaw ending on the high value.
[9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000]
=> 100

# 99 elements, one seesaw ending on the low value.
[500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500,501,500]
=> 99

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[4,3]
=> -1

@gen 4 small
[9998,9999]
=> 2

@gen 6 small
[5589,5587,5586,5587,5586,5587,5588]
=> 4

@gen 9 small
[9998,9999,9998,9999,9999,10000,10000]
=> 4

@gen 11 small
[254,255,254]
=> 3

@gen 12 small
[3,4,1]
=> 2

# Full size: 99 or 100 values; seed 4 is one seesaw over the whole row.
@gen 1
[9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9999,10000,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998,9999,9998]
=> 52

@gen 4
[1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2]
=> 100

@gen 26
[2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,3]
=> 84
